newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan Telecom sees merger aiding profits from 1998.
newsitem.headline: Japan Telecom sees merger aiding profits from 1998.

text.p: Japan Telecom Co, which is to merge with International Telecom Japan Co (ITJ) in October, said on Thursday that the planned merger will start contributing to Japan Telecom's profits in the year beginning April 1, 1998.
"We will concentrate on cutting costs in the current fiscal year by cutting duplicative operations at the two companies," a senior Japan Telecom official told a news conference.
ITJ is one of three international call operators in Japan.
Japan Telecom will increase its capital spending to 73 billion yen in 1997/98, up from 54.2 billion in 1996/97, to move into international and regional call services.
This amount of spending could exceed Japan Telecom's cash flow in fiscal 1997/98, the official said.
Japan Telecom also said it expected a parent operating profit of 43 billion yen in 1997/98.
